Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the collision you
reported. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just give you the facts of what happened, if that's all right.
Q: That's fine. For the record, can you confirm you were the driver of the vehicle involved?
A: Yes, I was driving my own car.
Q: Where were you when the collision occurred?
A: I was in Houston, Texas, at an intersection with a traffic signal. I was trying to make a left turn.
Q: Walk me through what you were doing just before impact.
A: I was waiting in the turn lane for a gap in oncoming traffic. When it looked clear, I started into the turn, and then a
vehicle coming straight through hit the front passenger side of my car.
Q: Did you see the other vehicle before you started your turn?
A: I saw headlights further back, but I thought there was enough room. I misjudged how fast it was coming.
Q: What was the signal showing for you when you began the turn?
A: It had changed to green for the through traffic, and my arrow had turned to a yield. I believed I could complete the
turn safely.
Q: Did you feel any pain or injury immediately afterward?
A: My shoulder hurt right away, mostly the right one. It got worse over the next day or so, and I've been having trouble
lifting my arm.
Q: Have you received medical treatment for that shoulder?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic and I've been referred for follow-up care.
Q: Is there anything you would like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I want to cooperate fully and get my vehicle and my medical situation sorted out.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.
"words_before" = the words written on the page directly before that date, copied exactly, that say
it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
